title: Our Relationship With Others Depends First on Our Relationship With Ourselves
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that external relationships are essentially a reflection of a person's internal self-regard, with self-trust, self-respect, and self-awareness forming the foundation of every genuine outside relationship. It focuses closely on self-talk as the mechanism, contrasting how positive inner dialogue builds confidence and openness with how negative self-talk — absolutist language like 'always' and 'never' — creates barriers and fuels misunderstanding in relationships with others. The piece uses concrete examples of self-talk ('I don't do anything right') and other-directed talk ('my partner never helps out') to show how the same distorted pattern damages both self-regard and outward relationships simultaneously. It closes with a direct call to examine one's own self-talk as the actual starting point for improving relationships with others.
points: External relationships are framed as a direct reflection of internal self-regard — self-trust, self-respect, and self-awareness are the stated foundation of genuine connection with others.
Positive self-talk is linked to confidence, emotional well-being, and openness; negative, absolutist self-talk ('always,' 'never') is linked to barriers and misunderstanding.
The same distorted thinking pattern shows up in both self-directed talk and talk about others, damaging both simultaneously.
The recommended starting point for better relationships is examining one's own inner dialogue, not the behavior of others.
quotes: As a rule, our external relationships reflect our internal state.
Self-trust, self-respect, and self-awareness form the core foundation for all genuine relationships.

On the other hand, negative self-talk, such as self-criticism, doubt, admonishment, and distorted thinking (like “always” and “never”), harms relationships by creating barriers, weakening conviction, and fueling misunderstandings.
Unhappiness on the inside produces unhappiness on the outside. That’s why our relationship with others depends enormously on our relationship with ourselves.
Examine your self-talk and the feelings you have about yourself. Perhaps it’s time for a tune-up.
